messages:
nova: Heads-up: hit a reproducible mid-stream auth tear in staging. Client keeps pushing, auth refresh happens, upstream rejects and frontdoor just drops the socket -> EPIPE on client. Quick repro below.

alex: Repro? env?

nova: Staging. Steps:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer short' https://frontdoor.redwood/api/stream -d @payload.json
# while stream active, rotate token for subject -> upstream rejects
```
Client sees a sudden connection close, no graceful error.

mira: We've discussed conn-lease and eager-gate already. I want to throw a different idea in: checkpoint-assisted delegation + auth-watermark.

sam: Explain the pattern.

mira: Sketch: frontdoor periodically emits signed stream-checkpoints (x-rdwl-checkpoint) that encode a watermark: last-ack-offset, subject, and auth-validation-timestamp. Checkpoint TTL short. If upstream later rejects midstream, frontdoor or upstream can issue a resume-hint tied to the latest checkpoint so client can resume from offset.

ingrid: So instead of binding a transient lease to the connection only, we persist small signed checkpoints that are safe to replay for resume semantics. That separates "auth continuity" from "live token policy".

nova: How does this help the auth-refresh case?

mira: If token refresh happens and upstream rejects a chunk, upstream can include x-rdwl-resume-from: <checkpoint-id> in trailers. Client SDK sees it and reconnects, sending resume token to continue from that offset. Frontdoor verifies checkpoint signature and enforces per-route resume_policy.

sam: Important: we must categorically disallow resume for write-intent streams unless route marks them idempotent. Also checkpoints must include a write-intent flag so frontdoor can refuse resume on non-idempotent streams.

alex: Tradeoffs: adds small storage (or HSM-signed opaque tokens) for checkpoints, requires client-sdk support, but avoids moving KMS trust to every upstream for token verification. Frontdoor signs checkpoints; upstream only needs to echo checkpoint id.

ingrid: Security considerations: checkpoints carry minimal authority. They must be single-use for write routes and bound to TLS session fingerprint + client-id to limit replay. TTL short (5-60s). Sign with a key that is auditable. Add checkpoint_issue and checkpoint_reuse metrics.

security-bot: Flagging: request a security micro-review for checkpoint token format and binding rules.

mira: Implementation sketch:
- frontdoor: emit x-rdwl-checkpoint: <base64(signed{offset,subject,timestamp,flags,conn_fingerprint})> every N frames or on accept
- upstream: on midstream auth rejection, return trailer x-rdwl-resume-checkpoint: <checkpoint-id> (or forward to frontdoor)
- client-sdk: on trailer, validate resume policy and reconnect with Resume-Checkpoint header
- config: route.resume_policy = none|resume_client|resume_server_trailer; route.resume_mode = read_only|idempotent_write|no_resume

sam: Metrics: checkpoint_issued, checkpoint_refused_on_resume, resume_success, resume_reject_nonidempotent. Logging: audit checkpoint issuance (no plaintext tokens in logs).

alex: Testing: unit tests for signing and fingerprint binding, integration test that rotates auth midstream and validates resume flow, chaos test toggling resume_policy. Also test garbage checkpoint replay attempts.

ingrid: Rollout plan: dark-launch checkpoints (emit header but ignore resume), collect metrics and abuse signals, then opt-in read-heavy routes. Coordinate client-sdk release for resume handling.

mira: Docs: clarify timeout semantics (if frontdoor emits checkpoint and continues, client-visible timeout unaffected). If eager-gate used, client waits until auth completes. Both behaviors must be explicit per-route.

nova: Action items:
- ingrid: draft RFC + sequence diagrams for checkpoint flow and fallback to eager-gate (ETA Thu)
- sam: inventory routes and classify resume_mode (ETA Tue)
- alex: sync with client-sdk owners for resume wire format (ETA Wed)
- mira: build staging harness that force-rotates auth midstream and validates resume (ETA Fri)

deploy-bot: feature-flag created in staging: frontdoor.checkpoint_resume (canary) :white_check_mark:

alex: Nice. Checkpoint approach feels like a good middle ground — less KMS expansion than conn-lease and more graceful for clients than eager-gate. Security review still required.
